children: By Staff Writer

Global iron ore prices have fallen about 20 percent from their early-summer peak of more than $110 per tonne, as weakness in China's construction sector continues to weigh on steel production and demand for the raw material, according to Swiss wealth manager Julius Baer.
“Prices are set to stay low, anchored by production costs in the high $80s and low $90s per tonne.” observed Carsten Menke, Head of Next Generation Research at Julius Baer, in a research note.
Despite record Chinese iron ore imports this year, much of the material has been stockpiled rather than consumed by steelmakers, he said.

China's steel production fell to its lowest level since 2018 during the first eight months of the year, reflecting continued weakness in the country's property and infrastructure sectors. However, Chinese steel exports have remained elevated, with their annualised run rate exceeding 110 million tonnes.
“Production would have been even lower were it not for exports,” he noted.
Menke said these exports were increasingly reaching neighbouring Asian markets, displacing domestic steel production and contributing to structural oversupply in the global steel market.
“That said, protectionist measures remain on the rise, resulting in globally dispersed steel prices,” he said, pointing out regional steel price differences.
Hot-rolled coil (HRC) prices are around $1,250 per tonne in the United States, compared with $830 in Europe, $550 in Japan and $490 in China, according to the report.

“While prices in the United States and Europe are heavily distorted by trade barriers, Japan is closest to a free market price,” explained Menke. “Structural imbalances are set to persist with China’s outsized exports and increasing trade barriers as the primary and secondary symptoms.”
The Julius Baer analyst expects global steel production to plateau, with growth in India offsetting declining output in China.
Lower demand
The increasing shift from blast furnaces to electric arc furnaces is also expected to reduce demand for iron ore.
Although seaborne iron ore supplies have likely peaked, Menke said available volumes should remain sufficient to keep prices relatively low.

“Depending on the Chinese traders’ willingness to pay and potential speculation about metals-intensive stimulus measures in the country, prices are likely to top out in the low $110s,” he noted adding that Such increases are likely to be short-lived because of sufficient seaborne supplies and weak profitability among Chinese steel producers.

In October 2025, UAE-based local English language newspaper Khaleej Times had reported that the Federal government has extended the increased customs duty from five per cent to 10 per cent on steel and steel coils until October 2026.

In June 2025, Saudi Arabia imposed final anti-dumping duties of 6.5 percent to 27.3 percent on imports of longitudinally welded circular steel and stainless steel pipes from China and Taiwan, effective 30 June 2025, for five years, according to a report by state-owned Saudi Press Agency (SPA).
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
